title: Schema migration synthetic event test harness design
content:
Purpose:
Generate deterministic and fuzz-style synthetic audit events to validate schema migrations, RBAC v2 enrichment, evidence linkage, and SIEM export plumbing across versions v1->v3. The harness is intended for: regression detection, false-positive/negative measurements, throughput/emulation tests, and automated CI gating for schema changes.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: event format variants (minimal/expanded), identity hashing permutations, evidence link formats, TTL/retention semantics, SIEM export flattening/transform rules, and consumer compatibility checks.
- Out of scope: production data ingestion, PII extraction from real records (we only use synthetic values), long-term archival of generated data.

Design principles:
1) Reproducible seeds: every test run takes an explicit seed so failing cases are reproducible.
2) Layered mutation pipeline: start with canonical templates, apply deterministic mutations, then randomized fuzz layers.
3) Version tagging: each event carries a migration_version vector (e.g., ["v1","rbac-v2-adj","evidence-link-v2"]) to exercise branching compatibility.
4) Consumer-focused assertions: validate both producer schema conformance and consumer deserialization behaviour (SIEM ingestion, analytics pipelines).
5) Privacy-by-design: no real PII; identifiers are synthetic but follow realistic entropy distributions.

Core components:
- Template library: canonical JSON event blueprints for major event classes: auth, permission-change, model-inference-call, evidence-upload, session-termination.
- Mutation engine: rule-based mutators (field rename, optional-field removal, type-coercion, enum-expansion) and stochastic mutators (length extremes, unicode, escaped control characters).
- Linkage simulator: constructs evidence chains across multiple events to test stitching and timeline reconstruction. Supports out-of-order emission, partial rehydration, and tombstone markers.
- Export adapters: light-weight adapters that simulate SIEM export transforms (flattening nested evidence, mapping enrichment fields, producing CSV/CEF-like outputs).
- Validator suite: schema-validator (JSON Schema + contract tests), consumer-runner (runs small consumer code to assert handling), and metrics collector.

Event templates (examples):
- minimal auth event template:
  { "event_id": "SYN-{{seed}}-auth-0001", "type": "auth.check", "ts": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z", "actor": { "id": "user:synthetic:1001", "role": "viewer" }, "outcome": "allow" }

- evidence upload (expanded) template:
  { "event_id": "SYN-{{seed}}-evidence-045", "type": "evidence.upload", "ts": "2026-03-01T12:01:12Z", "actor": { "id": "svc:synthetic:batch-3", "principals": ["svc:ingest"] }, "payload": { "evidence_id": "ev-{{uuid}}", "size_bytes": 4200, "mime": "application/json" }, "links": [ { "target_event": "SYN-{{seed}}-modelcall-001", "relation": "input_of" } ] }

Mutation rules (examples):
- rename_field(role -> rbac_role) applied to 10% of events to test tolerant deserialization.
- type_coercion on size_bytes (int -> string) to validate consumer defensive parsing.
- evidence_link_truncation: drop last 1-2 links to simulate partial ingestion.
- identity_hash_variants: actor.id replaced with stable-hash, salted-hash, and per-run ephemeral id.

Versioning and compatibility tests:
- forward-compat test: generate v2 events (new optional fields) and assert v1 consumers succeed with warnings.
- back-compat test: emit v1-only shaped events and ensure v3 mapping layer can rehydrate missing fields using enrichment heuristics.
- migration smoke: run a suite of 10k events with mixed versions and measure error rate <= 0.1% for parsing, <= 0.5% for downstream mapping mismatches.

SIEM export simulation:
- Flattening rules: nested payload.evidence -> evidence_id,evidence_mime,evidence_size columns.
- Field mapping: canonical "actor.id" -> "user" for legacy SIEM index; map "rbac_role" -> "user_role" when present.
- Sampling: support pre-export sampling (1%, 10%, 100%) and test sample representativeness across event classes.
- Bulk export throughput: adapters should simulate batch sizes up to 10k events/min and report serialization latency distribution.

Stitching and evidence lineage tests:
- multi-event chains: create chains of length 1..20 where each link has a random delivery delay and possible out-of-order arrival. Validate reconstruction yields correct chronology and that gaps are detected and surfaced.
- orphaned evidence detection: simulate events referencing nonexistent evidence and assert consumer raises a specific error class for downstream handling.

Metrics to collect per-run (CI-friendly):
- parse_error_rate (percent),
- consumer_deserialize_failures (count),
- mapping_mismatch_count,
- stitch_success_rate (percent),
- siem_export_serialization_latency_p50/p95/p99 (ms),
- synthetic_coverage_score (how many template variants exercised, 0..100).

Test scenarios (suggested suites):
1) Nominal: 2k events, mixed templates, 0% fuzz, validate 0 parse errors.
2) Conservative migration: include rename+optional fields, assert v1 consumers log warnings only.
3) Fuzz stress: 25k events with 15% stochastic mutations, measure p99 latency and parse_error_rate < 0.5%.
4) SIEM degrade: simulate export adapter failure modes (partial batch drop, malformed flattening) and assert retry/backpressure behaviour.
5) RBAC v2 enrichment: emit permission-change events and verify permission snapshot rehydration from rollback states.

CI and rollout integration:
- test harness lives in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-tests with a docker image for runners.
- Each schema change PR must include an acceptance test that runs the harness against both old and new contract definitions.
- Gate: merging a schema change requires no new critical failures and synthetic_coverage_score >= 85.

Operational runbook (short):
- When a migration PR is opened, trigger full harness with seed=commit-hash.
- If parse_error_rate > 0.1%: block rollout and debug failing templates.
- For SIEM export changes, run adapter simulator and check p99 latency delta < 30% vs baseline.

Appendix: sample failure fingerprints to surface in CI logs:
- "missing_field:evidence_id" (consumer cannot locate evidence link)
- "type_mismatch:size_bytes" (failed coercion)
- "stitch_gap:4" (4-event gap in reconstructed timeline)
- "siem_flatten:overflow" (field exceeded column length)

Next steps and open questions:
- Decide canonical migration_version encoding: single string vs array of tags. Proposal: array-of-tags for richer roll-forward rules.
- Add a mode to import small real-sanitized samples from production for distributional fidelity; legal review required.
- Define SLA for synthetic_test runtime in CI (target <= 8 minutes for acceptance runs).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an initial design focused on developer ergonomics and CI gating. We should prioritize fast, deterministic tests over exhaustive fuzzing in the short term.
- Cross-team ask: SRE to score the simulated export throughput against realistic egress limits; Product/CS to provide representative evidence link patterns from customer scenarios.

End of document.
